desktop.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: 4DTraveler Rome circa 500 BCE desktop bird's-eye overview.
Input image 1: project-owned Rome 125 CE image, EDIT TARGET for exact camera, geography, framing and material finish; architecture must be replaced with circa 500 BCE.
Primary request: Generate a richly detailed, realistic aerial interpretive reconstruction of early Republican Rome around 500 BCE. Make the transformation immediately visible: a compact low-rise archaic city amid open green land, exposed rolling hills, pasture, groves and fields. The city is already a substantial organized settlement, not a handful of prehistoric huts. Concentrate irregular one- and occasional two-storey plastered mudbrick and timber houses on tufa foundations, modest courtyards, russet terracotta roofs and some thatch around the Forum valley and hill slopes. Leave substantial unbuilt green land especially in the distant background and Campus Martius at left. Earth paths, garden plots, small agricultural holdings, sparse tiny historically dressed people, carts and small wooden river craft provide fine detail.
Geography and camera: retain the reference's 1586:992 landscape ratio, exact bird's-eye camera direction, entire crop and scale, no horizon. Preserve the Tiber sweeping through lower left, Palatine ridge at x .60 y .64, Capitoline rise near center-left, long Circus valley at lower right, and the location of the future Colosseum valley at x .855 y .38. Preserve geographic sites, NOT absent monuments. No zoom or reframing.
Historical transformation: Completely remove the Pantheon and its forecourt at x .12 y .51; show open Campus Martius terrain there. Remove Trajan's Forum, Column, Markets and the other Imperial Fora near x .43 y .37; restore a natural inhabited ridge/saddle between Capitoline and Quirinal instead of a flattened monumental complex. Remove Colosseum entirely at x .855 y .38 and replace it with a modest valley landscape, tracks, scattered early houses and gardens; no oval ruin, no Nero's lake. Remove imperial palaces from Palatine, replace with low archaic houses and sacred groves. Replace enormous Circus Maximus stone stands with a simple elongated open earthen racing ground in the same valley, only modest timber viewing areas, no giant stone stadium or marble spine. The young Roman Forum is a modest open civic space with simple archaic shrines and timber/terracotta structures, not imperial basilicas or colonnaded marble plazas.
Main landmark: On the Capitoline rise, a broad impressive but believable early Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on a tufa podium, deep columned front porch, wide red terracotta gabled roof, painted timber and terracotta ornament; Etrusco-Italic architectural character, not a white marble classical peripteral temple. This is the principal large building, not one of dozens of monumental complexes. Do not add a continuous later stone circuit wall.
Riverbanks: irregular earth, reeds, simple timber landings; remove the continuous imperial quays and all later stone arched bridges. Keep the river's reference location for visual registration.
Style: high-detail naturalistic architectural visualization, believable real scale, warm Mediterranean sunlight matching the reference, nuanced grass/soil/tufa/plaster/roof textures, realistic soft shadows and atmospheric distance. Read as a compelling landscape with a developing early city, substantially greener and less built up than 125 CE. No miniature tilt-shift blur.
Avoid: any Pantheon, Colosseum, domes, imperial fora, triumphal arches, aqueduct arcades, imperial baths or palaces, Christian or medieval buildings, modern elements, fantasy mountains, huge defensive walls, buildings from Greece or East Asia, text, dates, labels, border or watermark. Output only the complete finished landscape image.

Constraints: lock image 1's portrait camera and geographic frame while borrowing image 2's circa 500 BCE condition/style. No Colosseum, Pantheon, marble imperial architecture, medieval/christian buildings, modern features, fantasy mountains, East Asian architecture, text, labels, dates, borders or watermark.
